What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?
Answer/Official from LangSmith Remote MCP, LangSmith CLI, LangSmith MCP Server, Sandbox CLI, and the langsmith-cli README.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?

Short answer: yes, in both directions, and the CLI is the larger surface. Both read projects, traces, runs, threads, datasets, examples, and experiments — LangChain's own docs say the CLI "supports the same projects, traces, runs, datasets, experiments, and threads as the MCP server." Beyond that overlap, the Remote MCP uniquely offers typed prompt and billing tools plus zero-install OAuth from inside a client, while the CLI uniquely offers writes, exports, sandboxes, evaluators, Hub repos, agent tracing setup, and a raw REST escape hatch.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?
Typed prompt tools. list_prompts and get_prompt_by_name read prompts and templates. The CLI has no prompt command group at all — it can only reach prompts through langsmith api.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?
Billing usage. get_billing_usage returns organization trace counts for a date range, optionally filtered by workspace. There is no CLI billing command.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?
Nothing to install. A client connects with a URL and an OAuth login; no binary, no PATH, no self-update. That matters for hosted or sandboxed agents that cannot install software.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?
Model-driven tool selection. Tools arrive in the model's context with schemas, so the agent picks and fills them itself instead of an agent-authored shell command being parsed and executed.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?

Character-budget pagination. get_thread_history and fetch_runs page by character count (max_chars_per_page, preview_chars) so a response fits a context window. The CLI's equivalent is --limit / --offset plus detail flags — item-based, not size-based.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?
Sandboxes. langsmith sandbox builds snapshots from Docker images, boots VMs, runs exec, opens interactive consoles, and tunnels TCP ports into a sandbox. No MCP tool touches sandboxes.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?

Evaluator management. langsmith evaluator upload uploads code evaluators as offline (dataset) or online (project) rules, with --sampling-rate and --replace; evaluator list and evaluator delete round it out. Compare LangSmith/Evaluator and LangSmith/Evaluator/Online.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?

Real writes and deletes. dataset create / delete / upload, example create / delete. The MCP's create_dataset, update_examples, push_prompt, and run_experiment are documentation-only tools — they return instructions on how to do the thing, not the thing itself.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?
Bulk export to disk. trace export, run export (JSONL), dataset export, and the global -o <path>. MCP tools return payloads into a conversation, capped by the character budget.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?
LangSmith/Engine issues. langsmith project issues list --project <name> lists Engine-detected issues.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?

Raw REST escape hatch. langsmith api is a gh api-style authenticated wrapper over the whole LangSmith REST API, with langsmith api ls / api info to browse the OpenAPI spec. This makes the CLI a strict superset in reach: anything the API exposes, including endpoints behind MCP tools, is callable.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?
Hub repos. langsmith hub init / push / pull / list / get / delete manage versioned agent and skill repos on the LangSmith Hub.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?

Tracing coding agents. langsmith trace setup claude and langsmith trace setup codex write Claude/Code and Codex config and install the tracing plugin so the agent's own sessions land in a LangSmith project.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?
Shell-native ergonomics. --format pretty tables, the filter DSL via --filter, --show-hierarchy run trees, --min-latency / --min-tokens filters, named profiles, and pipes into jq.
What can the LangSmith/MCP/Remote do that the LangSmith/CLI can't, and vice versa?
Works where MCP OAuth doesn't. The docs explicitly route Codex users to the CLI because Codex's OAuth flow is incompatible with the Remote MCP.

Use the Remote MCP when an agent should discover LangSmith capabilities on its own with no install step, or when prompts and billing are the target. Use the CLI when the task involves writing, exporting, sandboxes, evaluators, or anything scripted — and note that langsmith api means the CLI can eventually do everything the MCP can, while the reverse is not true.

As of October 8, 2026, there is no official LangChain CLI command, Terraform resource, Pulumi resource, MCP tool, or known community package that declaratively manages Agent Server assistants across LangSmith Deployments. I also found no dedicated public assistants-as-code tool on GitHub, PyPI, or npm that exports/imports/diffs/reconciles assistants between LangSmith deployment hostnames. The only first-party automation surface with complete assistant lifecycle support is the Agent Server /assistants REST API and the official Python/TypeScript LangGraph SDKs.
LangGraph Assistants as Code in LangSmith Deployments
That distinction matters because LangSmith now has three separate layers that use similar vocabulary:
LangGraph Assistants as Code in LangSmith Deployments
1. A graph is the deployed code/blueprint registered through langgraph.json.
LangGraph Assistants as Code in LangSmith Deployments
2. An Agent Server assistant is a versioned binding of that graph to config, context, metadata, name, etc. It is persisted as Agent Server data and managed under /assistants.
LangGraph Assistants as Code in LangSmith Deployments

3. A newer LangSmith agent is a workspace/control-plane identity used to organize tracing and deployment environments such as development, staging, and production. Binding a deployment to an agent_id and environment does not replace the Agent Server assistant abstraction: LangChain's current deployment documentation explicitly says that after deployment, execution still uses “assistants for configuration, threads for state, and runs for workloads.”
LangGraph Assistants as Code in LangSmith Deployments
For your use case, the practical answer is therefore:
LangGraph Assistants as Code in LangSmith Deployments
Keep assistant specifications and fixed UUIDs in Git and run your own small reconciler against each deployment's Agent Server API.
LangGraph Assistants as Code in LangSmith Deployments

That is not merely a workaround around a better declarative product that I found; today it is the missing product layer. The official API has nearly everything needed to implement it cleanly, including caller-selected assistant_id, idempotent create with if_exists: "do_nothing", updates that create versions, version listing, and set_latest. What it lacks is a native desired-state/diff/import/export abstraction.

There is no built-in diff, export, import, sync, plan, or Terraform-style reconciliation method in the documented assistants clients. Pulumi has no dedicated LangSmith provider in its Registry. Pulumi's registry does offer Any Terraform Provider, currently listed at v1.4.0 from August 14, 2026, which can consume a Terraform provider dynamically. That means you can use LangChain's Terraform provider through Pulumi infrastructure code, but this cannot manufacture an assistant resource that is absent from the upstream provider schema. It therefore adds zero additional assistant capability.

There are three things that can be confused here.

The original standalone LangSmith MCP Server exposed LangSmith conversation history, prompt management, traces/runs, datasets/examples, experiments/evaluations, and billing. Version 0.1.1 shipped February 25, 2026. LangChain subsequently archived the GitHub repository on August 14, 2026 and directs users toward the hosted Remote MCP service. It had no documented Agent Server assistant CRUD.
LangGraph Assistants as Code in LangSmith Deployments

The newer LangSmith Remote MCP similarly exposes LangSmith management/observability tools, not a deployment's /assistants resource. It supports interactive OAuth and programmatic API-key authentication.

Finally, an Agent Server itself can expose an MCP endpoint, but that endpoint is for presenting the deployed agent as an MCP-accessible tool; it is not an assistant administration protocol. LangChain's current Managed Deep Agents documentation, for example, describes deployment as producing an Agent Server including its API and MCP endpoint, while assistant lifecycle remains part of Agent Server's normal API.
LangGraph Assistants as Code in LangSmith Deployments
So none of LangChain's MCP options is an assistants-as-code manager.
